recipes.name: Palak Paneer (Spinach and Cottage Cheese Curry)
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is rich in iron from spinach and provides protein and calcium from paneer, which may support healthy hemoglobin levels and bone density, addressing the influencing factors of hemoglobin and calcium intake.
instructions: Blanch spinach in hot water for 2-3 minutes, then immediately transfer to ice water. Drain and blend into a smooth puree.
Heat mustard oil in a pan. Add finely chopped onion and sauté until golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato and cook until soft and pulpy.
Stir in cumin powder, coriander powder, and turmeric powder. Cook for 2 minutes until spices are fragrant.
Add the spinach puree and water, mix well. Bring to a simmer.
Add paneer cubes and salt. Cook for 5-7 minutes.
Stir in garam masala. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Mackerel Fish Curry
recipes.health_benefit: This curry is an excellent source of Omega-3 fatty acids, which may help improve triglyceride and HDL cholesterol levels, and Vitamin D, directly addressing key influencing factors. It also provides lean protein.
instructions: Clean and cut mackerel fillets into pieces. Marinate with a pinch of turmeric and salt for 10 minutes.
Heat mustard oil in a pot. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves and slit green chilies, sauté for a minute.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add ginger-garlic paste and cook until the raw smell disappears.
Add turmeric powder, red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder. Sauté for 2 minutes on low heat, adding a splash of water if needed.
Add tomato puree and cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Add tamarind pulp, coconut milk, water, and salt. Bring the gravy to a gentle simmer.
Carefully add the marinated fish pieces. Cover and cook on low heat for 8-10 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through. Avoid stirring too vigorously.
Serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: Indian Style Chicken & Veggie Stir-fry
recipes.health_benefit: This dish provides lean protein for satiety and muscle maintenance, along with diverse vitamins, minerals, and fiber from various vegetables. It is low in unhealthy fats, which could help in managing triglyceride and cholesterol levels, and supports stable blood sugar.
instructions: Heat oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Add sliced onion, ginger-garlic paste, and green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add chicken strips and stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add carrots and broccoli florets, stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Add bell peppers, turmeric powder, and cumin powder. Stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes.
Pour in soy sauce and vinegar, season with black pepper and salt.
Toss everything together for a final minute. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with quinoa or brown rice.

recipes.name: Moong Dal Cheela with Mixed Vegetable Raita
recipes.health_benefit: This meal is high in protein and fiber from moong dal, which can aid in satiety and help manage blood sugar levels (HbA1c, glucose). The raita provides probiotics for gut health and calcium, supporting overall wellness.
instructions: For Cheela: Drain the soaked moong dal. Blend it with green chili, ginger, cumin seeds, turmeric powder, and salt, adding minimal water to form a smooth, thick batter. Heat a non-stick tawa and lightly grease it with oil. Pour a ladleful of batter and spread evenly. Drizzle oil, cook until golden brown, then flip and cook the other side.
For Raita: In a bowl, whisk the low-fat yogurt until smooth. Add grated cucumber, chopped tomato, chopped onion (if using), roasted cumin powder, black salt, and fresh coriander. Mix well.
Serve hot moong dal cheelas with the refreshing vegetable raita.

recipes.name: Oats Upma with Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: This dish is high in soluble fiber from oats, which could help in managing cholesterol levels (triglycerides, LDL) and blood glucose, contributing to overall cardiovascular health and stable energy levels.
instructions: Lightly dry roast the rolled oats in a pan for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Set aside.
Heat rice bran oil in the same pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves and slit green chili, sauté for a few seconds.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add chopped carrot and peas. Cook for 3-5 minutes until vegetables are slightly tender.
Add turmeric powder and mix well. Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, add the roasted oats, and stir continuously to prevent lumps. Cover and cook on low heat for 3-5 minutes, or until all the water is absorbed and oats are cooked.
Stir in lemon juice. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with a dollop of low-fat yogurt.

recipes.name: Rajma Curry (Kidney Bean Curry)
recipes.health_benefit: Rajma is an excellent source of plant-based protein, dietary fiber, and iron. This dish can help in maintaining stable blood sugar levels (HbA1c, glucose) and supporting digestive health, while also contributing to hemoglobin levels.
instructions: Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, and cinnamon stick. Let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add tomato puree and cook until the oil separates. Stir in turmeric powder, red chili powder, and coriander powder. Sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add the boiled rajma along with some of its cooking water. Add salt and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. Mash a few rajma beans to thicken.
Stir in garam masala. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with brown rice.

recipes.name: Besan Cheela
recipes.health_benefit: As a good source of plant-based protein and fiber, besan cheela can help promote satiety and contribute to stable blood sugar levels, addressing the influencing factors of HbA1c and glucose.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine besan, chopped onion, tomato, green chili, fresh coriander, ginger-garlic paste, cumin powder, turmeric powder, and salt.
Gradually add water, whisking continuously to form a smooth, lump-free batter of pouring consistency.
Heat a non-stick tawa over medium heat and lightly grease it with oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the hot tawa and spread it evenly in a circular motion to form a thin cheela. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.
Cook until golden brown and crisp on one side, then flip and cook the other side.
Repeat for the remaining batter. Serve hot with green chutney or low-fat yogurt.
